candidate_title: Staged multi-key write batch with atomic commit, rollback and crash recovery for a SQLite-backed disk cache
scenario_goal: Let an application stage several cache writes (set/add/delete/touch/incr) and make them become visible as one unit only when the batch exits successfully. Before commit, the staged writes are invisible to every other cache handle and process; on exception, explicit rollback, or process crash mid-batch, the cache must return to its pre-batch state and leave no orphaned value files behind.
actors: A writer thread or process opening a batch on a cache directory
Other processes and other cache handles reading and writing the same directory concurrently
A crash or hard exit that kills the process between staging a value and committing it
The cache reopened later, which must discard any unfinished batch
domain_objects: The cache key/value index persisted in SQLite
Value files stored on disk and referenced by index rows
A staging area that holds pending writes for the current batch
Per-key metadata: expire time, tag, size, mode, filename
Aggregate views: item count, total volume, iteration order, statistics
workflow: Open a batch on a cache handle
Issue arbitrary mixes of writes and deletes, including deleting then re-setting the same key and setting then deleting it
Read inside the batch and observe the staged state while other handles observe the committed state
Exit the batch: success commits every staged change at once; an exception discards them
Reopen the cache after a crash and observe that the unfinished batch is discarded
state_and_lifecycle: A pending write is neither visible nor counted until commit
Commit moves every staged row into the live index inside one transaction and releases superseded files
Rollback removes staged rows and the files they own
An unfinished batch found at open time is rolled back before the cache is used
Expiration, tag eviction and culling only apply to committed rows; staged rows join them after commit
conflicts_failures_recovery: Two processes open batches on the same directory at the same time and commit independently
A process crashes after staging files but before commit; files must be reclaimed
A crash in the middle of commit must not leave a half-applied batch
Concurrent independent writes outside the batch must not be blocked by an open batch
Nesting a batch inside a batch must raise a clear error instead of silently merging
observable_outcomes: Batch commit makes every staged key visible at the same instant; rollback leaves none of them
A second cache handle sees nothing until commit
Item count and total volume change only after commit
Expired and tagged keys written in a batch behave like ordinary keys after commit
The consistency checker reports no unknown files after any rollback or crash
verifier_behaviors: Distinguish real atomic commit/rollback from writes that leak visibility early
Distinguish correct crash recovery from implementations that leave orphan files or half-applied rows
Distinguish correct staging from implementations that block or corrupt concurrent writers
Check that aggregate views ignore staged rows and that expiration and tag eviction apply after commit
Re-check a fixed set of existing single-key behaviours so they do not regress
task_difficulties: Choosing where staged writes live so that reads inside the batch see them while every other handle and process does not, and so that commit is a single atomic transition
Ordering file writes, index updates and old-file deletion so that a crash at any point leaves a state that reopening can repair without orphan files or half-applied rows
Keeping staged writes out of expiration, tag eviction, culling, counting and volume until commit, then making them join all of those at once, including delete-then-set and set-then-delete on one key
